legislation.value: Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Minimum Tax for Multinational Enterprise Groups) Ordinance 2025 (Ord. No. 21 of 2025), adding Part 4AA and Schedules 61–64 to the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112)

enactment.value: Enacted 6 June 2025 (per IRD). Comes into operation on the day of publication in the Gazette.
enactment.note: The Gazette copy shows the Chief Executive's signature dated 5 June 2025.

headlineCitRate.value: 16.5% (corporations). Two-tiered: 8.25% on the first HK$2m of assessable profits.

domesticTopUpTax.value: HKMTT, designed as a QDMTT. It charges top-up tax on low-taxed HK constituent entities in priority to the IIR and UTPR.

QDMTT.value: Payable for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025

IIR.value: Payable for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2025

UTPR.value: Not yet in force. Starts for fiscal years beginning on or after a date the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury will specify by Gazette notice.

QDMTTSafeHarbour.value: QDMTT Safe Harbour: Yes, from 1 January 2025

filing.who: Each HK constituent entity, or one designated local entity (appointed annually)
filing.value: Within 6 months after the last day of the reporting fiscal year, filed electronically via the Pillar Two Portal

filing.obligation: Top-up tax return (GloBE + HKMTT, including GIR information)
filing.who: Each HK constituent entity, or one designated local entity. The GIR section is relieved if the GIR is filed in a jurisdiction that exchanges it with HK under a qualifying competent authority agreement.
filing.value: Within 15 months after the last day of the reporting fiscal year (18 months for the first transition year)

filing.obligation: Payment of top-up tax (per notice of assessment)
filing.value: One month after the later of the return filing deadline or the date of the notice of assessment. No provisional top-up tax.

registration.value: Apply for a group code (MNE code / JV code) on paper Form IR1485, needed to file the top-up tax notification
The notifying entity registers a dedicated Business Tax Portal (BTP) business account to access the Pillar Two Portal
Authorised signers must use an e-Cert (Organisational) with AEOI Functions

safeHarbours.value: Transitional CbCR Safe Harbour, Transitional UTPR Safe Harbour, QDMTT Safe Harbour, and Simplified Calculations Safe Harbour for non-material constituent entities

appliesToIir.value: Enacted. Under Sch. 61 Pt 3 Div. 2 s.4 IRO, the group's jurisdictional top-up tax under the GloBE rules (IIR/UTPR) is taken to be zero if a test is met in the transition period.

appliesToDomestic.value: Not expressly stated. The TCSH in Sch. 61 Pt 3 deems the top-up tax under the GloBE rules to be zero. Sch. 62 s.4 computes HKMTT by applying the GloBE rules (Chapter 2 excepted), and 'GloBE rules' is defined as Parts 1–2 of Sch. 61. Whether the Part 3 TCSH also zeroes HKMTT is not stated in the Ordinance or on the IRD page.
appliesToDomestic.note: The engine assumes the TCSH also applies to HKMTT (consistent with OECD guidance for QDMTTs) and flags this in the trail. Confirm against IRD guidance or the HKMTT return when published.

enactedPeriod.value: Transition period: all FYs beginning on or before 31 Dec 2026, excluding any FY ending after 30 Jun 2028 (Sch. 61 Pt 3 Div. 2 s.2(1)).

extension.value: OECD one-year extension (SbS Package, Jan 2026) not yet adopted in Hong Kong law. Schedules 61/64 can be amended by notice under s.26AG; no such notice or IRD announcement was found.
extension.note: Absence of evidence as at 2026-10-06 (IRD GMT page and Ord. No. 21 of 2025 checked). Re-check the Gazette and the IRD page.

portal.value: Pillar Two Portal Phase 1 (notifications) launched 19 Jan 2026. Phase 2 (top-up tax returns, e-assessments) stated for Q4 2026.

localFeatures.title: Designated local entity (filing)
localFeatures.value: HK constituent entities can designate one HK constituent entity, appointed annually, to file the notification and the top-up tax return for all of them.

localFeatures.title: Designated paying entity and joint liability
localFeatures.value: By default, HKMTT is allocated across HK constituent entities in proportion to GloBE income. A group can designate one or more paying entities. If a designated payer does not pay, all HK constituent entities become jointly and severally liable.

localFeatures.title: Territorial (source-based) profits tax
localFeatures.value: Profits tax is charged only on profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong. No tax is levied on profits arising abroad, even if remitted to Hong Kong.

localFeatures.title: Territorial regime × HKMTT (analysis)
localFeatures.value: HKMTT follows GloBE mechanics: jurisdictional ETR is computed on aggregate GloBE income and adjusted covered taxes. Offshore-sourced profits that bear no HK profits tax can therefore lower the HK GloBE ETR and create HKMTT exposure.
localFeatures.note: Our inference from IRD's description of the GloBE/HKMTT mechanics, not an IRD statement. Confirm against IRD guidance and the facts of the group.

localFeatures.title: Investment entities excluded from HKMTT
localFeatures.value: Investment entities and insurance investment entities are excluded from HKMTT to preserve their tax neutrality.

localFeatures.title: Top-up tax deemed profits tax
localFeatures.value: Top-up tax is deemed profits tax, so existing collection and objection/appeal machinery applies and CDTA mutual agreement procedures can be used. The objection period is 2 months from the notice of assessment.

localFeatures.title: HK resident entity definition (retrospective)
localFeatures.value: A new 'Hong Kong resident entity' definition (incorporated in HK, or normally managed or controlled in HK) applies retrospectively from 1 January 2024.

localFeatures.title: Mandatory e-filing of profits tax returns
localFeatures.value: Entities of in-scope MNE groups must e-file profits tax returns (BIR51/BIR52) for years of assessment beginning on or after 1 April 2025 ('once-in, always-in').

localFeatures.title: No QRTC regime (yet)
localFeatures.value: On submissions asking for a qualified refundable tax credit regime, the Government said it needs to carefully consider feasibility given the policy and fiscal implications.
localFeatures.note: LegCo Panel on Financial Affairs paper, October 2024. Check for later announcements.

localFeatures.title: GIR MCAA signed
localFeatures.value: Hong Kong signed the GIR MCAA on 21 April 2026, enabling central GIR filing and exchange.
